research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register text (12 FR 2067, issue of March 29, 1947) is headed Executive Order 9837, Regulations Governing the Transfer of Leave Between the Foreign Service and Other Government Agencies, and is signed Harry S. Truman, The White House, March 27, 1947. I read the whole order; it has four numbered paragraphs and the held representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12292 (1981). The dossier chain also lists Executive Order 9452 of 1944, but that order predates this one and the held record under that number is the 1981 Federal Register page range that contains Executive Order 12292, so it supplies no event. A search of the held texts for this order's number found only Executive Order 12292 and held copies of the same 1981 pages. The order states no own-terms end.
savings_reason: Executive Order 12292 was searched in full for saving, transition, continuation and accrual words and contains none, so nothing in its held text continues leave-transfer rules after the revocation. Accrued leave transfers made before 1981 are consequences already carried out; no held source shows any of them depending on this order's continued force.
earlier_end_check: The order contains no fixed end date, no sunset and no condition; its only date language is paragraph 4, which makes the order effective as of November 13, 1946. No held order text names Executive Order 9837 other than Executive Order 12292 and the copies of its Federal Register pages, so no earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end is found in the held corpus.
scope_check: Four clauses are inventoried, one per numbered paragraph: the required transfer of all leave up to the receiving agency's maximum (paragraph 1), the five-work-day to seven-calendar-day equivalence (paragraph 2), the construction of the quoted limit in section 935 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 (paragraph 3) and the effective-as-of statement (paragraph 4). The recitals and signature block are not operative. Executive Order 12292 revokes the order as a whole by number, so every clause ends on the same date.
independent_command_check: No paragraph is a delegation or standing rule that survives the order: each regulates leave transfers under sections 934(b) and 935 of the 1946 Act and is part of this order's text. The statute itself is a separate source of law that an executive order cannot revoke, and the claim does not assert that the statute ended.
savings_check: Executive Order 12292 contains no saving or transition provision in its held text; no residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search.
